title: DOM helpers (no-flash)
summary: Element builder and in-place patch helpers used by every UI file: el, q, mountOnce, patchList (keyed reconcile), setText/setClass/setHidden/setValue and friends, reserve, swapMedia, delayedIndicator, revealApp. The safe no-innerHTML pattern behind the zero-flash law.
description: Build a subtree once with `el(html)` or `mountOnce(host, html)` (which throws if the host already has children), then patch with the `set*` helpers, which write only when the value differs, and `patchList` for keyed lists (update, insert, remove; never clear and refill). `setValue` refuses to overwrite a focused field. `revealApp` flips `body.app-ready` after first content and tells the Tauri shell `app_ready`. `el`, `mountOnce` and `setHtml` do assign innerHTML, but only on fresh detached nodes or an empty host.
statusReason: seeded from B06 for the owner to confirm

exports.signature: export type Disposer = () => void
exports.doc: A function that cancels or dismisses what a helper started.

exports.signature: export function delayedIndicator(show: () => void, hide: () => void, delay = 300, minVisible = 250): Disposer
exports.doc: Show an indicator only if the wait outlasts `delay`; once visible keep it for at least `minVisible` so it cannot blink. Returns the dismiss function. The app's own numbers: 300 / 250.

exports.signature: export function pendingClass(el: HTMLElement, delay = 300, minVisible = 250): Disposer
exports.doc: Convenience over delayedIndicator for an element that carries .ns-pending: toggles .is-shown so the element keeps its reserved box while hidden.

exports.signature: export interface PatchListOptions<T> { key: (item: T) => string; create: (item: T) => HTMLElement; update: (node: HTMLElement, item: T) => void; }
exports.doc: The three callbacks patchList needs: a stable key, a node factory and an in-place updater.

exports.signature: export function patchList<T>(container: HTMLElement, items: T[], opts: PatchListOptions<T>): void
exports.doc: Reconcile `container`'s children against `items` by key. Existing nodes are updated in place (scroll, focus, selection, in-progress input survive); missing nodes are created; extra nodes are removed;

exports.signature: export function swapMedia(img: HTMLImageElement, nextSrc: string): Promise<void>
exports.doc: Replace an image's source without a blank frame: decode off-screen, then swap src in one write. The old picture stays visible until the new one can paint. Resolves when the swap happened, rejects on load failure.

exports.signature: export function setText(el: Element | null, text: string): void
exports.doc: Write text only when it differs. Numeric readouts should also carry .ns-tabular and a reserved width so neighbours never shift.

exports.signature: export function setClass(el: Element | null, cls: string, on: boolean): void
exports.doc: Toggle a class only when the state differs (no attribute churn).

exports.signature: export function reserve(el: HTMLElement, box: { width?: number; height?: number; minHeight?: number; aspect?: string }): void
exports.doc: Reserve a box before content lands. Pass width/height in px or an aspect ratio string like '16 / 9'.

exports.signature: export function revealApp(): void
exports.doc: The app's boot reveal: #app is visibility:hidden from the critical inline style; call this exactly once after the first render is in the DOM. Two frames so fonts and layout settle before the single reveal.

exports.signature: export function mountOnce(host: HTMLElement, html: string): void
exports.doc: Mount a fresh subtree from a template string ONCE into an empty host. Refuses to overwrite a host that already has rendered children, which is the exact mistake the zero-flash law forbids; patch it instead.

exports.signature: export function el<T extends HTMLElement = HTMLElement>(html: string): T
exports.doc: Parses a template string into one detached element; the way to build a node once.

exports.signature: export function q<T extends Element = HTMLElement>(root: ParentNode, sel: string): T
exports.doc: querySelector that throws when the element is missing, so a wrong selector fails loudly.

exports.signature: export function setHidden(node: HTMLElement, hidden: boolean): void
exports.doc: Sets node.hidden only when it differs.

exports.signature: export function setDisabled(node: HTMLButtonElement | HTMLInputElement | HTMLSelectElement, disabled: boolean): void
exports.doc: Sets disabled on a button, input or select only when it differs.

exports.signature: export function setTitle(node: HTMLElement, title: string): void
exports.doc: Sets the tooltip title only when it differs.

exports.signature: export function setStyleVar(node: HTMLElement, name: string, value: string): void
exports.doc: Sets one inline custom property only when its value differs.

exports.signature: export function setValue(node: HTMLInputElement | HTMLSelectElement, value: string): void
exports.doc: Sets a field value only when it differs and the field is not focused.

exports.signature: export function setChecked(node: HTMLInputElement, on: boolean): void
exports.doc: Sets a checkbox state only when it differs.

exports.signature: export function setHtml(node: Element, html: string, key: string): void
exports.doc: Replaces a node content from a template string, but only when the key differs from the last one rendered.

exports.signature: export function escapeHtml(s: string): string
exports.doc: Escapes & < > " and apostrophe for use in template strings.

exports.signature: export const isMac
exports.doc: True on macOS and iOS platforms.

invariants.text: Build a node once, then patch text, classes, hidden flags and lists in place. Never assign innerHTML or clear textContent on a live container to rebuild it, and reserve space so nothing shifts when content arrives.
Every set* helper compares before writing; call sites must use them instead of assigning textContent, hidden, value or class directly on a live node.
